dhp363:2: _Manta_ can refer to sacred recitations (“mantras”), however the more common meaning is “advice, counsel.” _Anuddhata_ can also mean “not agitated” - so this line could be rendered “who is not agitated when giving advice.”
dhp368:3: _Pada_ can also mean “location,” in which case this could be rendered “arrives at the place of peace” or simply “reaches peace.”
dhp368:4: _Saṅkhārūpasama_ is the “tranquility” (_upasama_) of all “things” (_saṅkhāra_). For ease of reading this is rendered here simply as “complete tranquility.”
dhp370:1: Perhaps the five hindrances and the five lower fetters?
dhp370:4: A common metaphor for attaining awakening.
dhp374:1: _Sammasati_ (lit. “completely touches”) here means to directly and personally experience.
